NFL Paris 2026: Aaron Rodgers leads Pittsburgh Steelers past New Orleans Saints in first-ever game in France
The Pittsburgh Steelers beat the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in the first-ever NFL regular-season game to be played in Paris; Aaron Rodgers passes Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history
Sunday 25 October 2026 17:17, UK
Aaron Rodgers overtook Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history as the Pittsburgh Steelers beat the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the first regular-season game to be played in Paris, France.
The four-time MVP quarterback surpassed Manning's tally of 539 touchdown passes with a first-half strike to tight end Darnell Washington and finished the game 19 of 30 for 212 yards as Mike McCarthy's Steelers improved to 5-2 on the year.
Saints quarterback Tyler Shough went 30 of 38 for 278 yards, a touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele and a second-half interception as Kellen Moore's side, honouring their deep-rooted French ties this week, dropped to 2-5.
Pittsburgh's Terrible Towels flew proudly while travelling Saints translated NOLA noise to Europe as the Stade de France welcomed 78,488 fans for the sixth of nine international games this season, Paris one of three first-time hosts for 2026 alongside Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro.
Civil unrest in France had dominated build-up to Sunday's game after what began as peaceful demonstrations had turned into violence and looting, resulting in the cancellation of fan events and prompting an increased security presence across the city.
Still, an undeterred crowd would serenade more NFL history with another electric atmosphere reflect of the league's reach overseas, albeit bolstered by a significant travelling party from both Pittsburgh and New Orleans.

Chris Boswell was a perfect three of three on field goals, while Saints counterpart Daniel Carlson was guilty of a costly miss.
Trailing 13-10 at the break, the Saints saw their immediate reply come up empty when Shough was intercepted by Payton Wilson to end a 14-play drive lasting that had knocked a costly seven-and-a-half minutes off the clock.
Young kept his team alive on the ensuing possession when the Saints sack leader swarmed Rodgers to stall the drive on third-and-10, Boswell coming out to kick a 39-yard field goal.
The Saints, though, were denied a chance to cut into Pittsburgh's lead again when Daniel Carlson missed a 52-yard field goal with 10 minutes remaining. Carlson had notably arrived in Paris on his own late this week, with his wife due to give birth back home.
Boswell had delivered the first ever points scored in Paris with a 28-yard field goal at the end of Pittsburgh's opening drive, before giving his team a 13-10 lead with his 47-yard effort as time expired in the second quarter.
Carlson drew the Saints level at 3-3 with a 38-yard field goal after Shough had flipped the field with a 49-yard strike to Barion Brown.
Pittsburgh tight end Washington scored the first-ever touchdown in Paris when he treated the French crowd to a tinge of Randy Moss while out-muscling a helpless Kool-Aid McKinstry for a four-yard grab at the side of the end zone. His exhibition in bully ball would see Rodgers join Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history.
Rodgers himself had teed up the touchdown beautifully with a 51-yard strike to DK Metcalf after climbing the the pocket and launching deep on the move to convert on third-and-14.
Shough capped his side's response with a one-yard touchdown pass to Vele inside the two-minute warning after the Saints had been stuffed at the one-yard line for three straight plays.
What did they say...
Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy: "I would say it overshadowed the game, I know a lot of our team had families in France. With the uncertainty Saturday we stayed close to the hotel. France is a beautiful place, I'd love the opportunity to come back and enjoy it."
Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers: "I've enjoyed the last two international games (Ireland and France), and then obviously London. For a long time in Green Bay we never got to go overseas because they were never going to give up a home game and then we did in 2022. I've enjoyed it, I wish we could have enjoyed it both in Ireland and France for a little more time. It's great the game is growing."
Stats leaders:
Pittsburgh Steelers
- Passing: Aaron Rodgers, 19/30, 212 yards, 1 TD
- Rushing: Jaylen Warren, 18 carries, 101 yards
- Receiving: DK Metcalf, 2 catches, 56 yards
New Orleans Saints
- Passing: Tyler Shough, 30/38, 278 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT
- Rushing: Tyler Shough, 3 carries, 7 yards
- Receiving: Alvin Kamara, 7 catches, 57 yards

הפיטסבורג סטילרס ניצחו 10-16 את הניו אורלינס סיינטס באצטדיון סטאד דה פראנס, במסגרת משחק העונה הסדירה הראשון בהיסטוריה של ליגת ה-NFL שהתקיים בפריז, צרפת. הקוורטרבק הוותיק אהרון רודגרס עקף את פייטון מאנינג במקום הטיטולרי לשaring במספר מסירות הטאצ'דাউন השלישי בהיסטוריה של הליגה, כשהגיע ל-540 מסירות מוצלחות לאחר מסירה לדארנל וושינגטון במחצית הראשונה. רודגרס סיים את המשחק עם 212 יארד והעלה את מאזן קבוצתו תחת אימונו של מייק מקארתי ל-5-2.

מנגד, קוורטרבק הסיינטס טיילר שו רשם 278 יארד ומסירת טאצ'דאון אחת לדבון וילה, אך גם ספג חטיפה אחת, והקבוצה ירדה למאזן 2-5. המשחק משך אליו קהל ענק של למעלה מ-78 אלף צופים באווירה חגיגית, זאת על אף ההתרחשויות האלימות והמחאות שקדמו לאירוע ברחבי צרפת ואילצו הידוק אבטחתי ניכר סביב הבירה. הבעיטות של כריס בוסוול מדויקות העניקו יתרון קריטי לפיטסבורג, בזמן שדניאל קרלסון מהסיינטס החמיץ בעיטה קריטית לקראת הסיום שאפשרה לסטילרס לשמור על היתרון עד לסיום.
